references.text: Jesus' claim to be God is met with an accusation of blasphemy, but he responds by quoting the Book of Psalms where it says that humans can be called 'gods' because they receive God's word. This shows that the accusation against Jesus is misunderstood when one considers how Hebrew Scripture uses the term.

Isaiah emphasizes that there is only one true God, which underlies the Jewish accusation that Jesus makes himself God. At the same time, the prophet points to God's eternity and uniqueness, a theme Jesus challenges and fulfills in his identity.

In this early encounter with Jewish leaders, Jesus calls God his own Father, leading them to understand that he is making himself equal to God. This is the direct precursor to the accusation of blasphemy in John 10:33.
The Jews repeat the accusation of blasphemy by saying that Jesus makes himself God's Son, confirming that their main opposition to him throughout the Gospel concerns his claimed equality with God.
